summary: L-4 cab on a 9,954 ft White Cloud peak in Sawtooth NRA: built 1933, emergency use from the 1970s, saved and restored 1985-89, NHLR-listed 2016.

access.note: Summit reached on foot by a difficult five-mile (one-way) trail; no rental or overnight use for the cab found in the sources read. Lookout is on emergency status.

visit.trail_note: Five miles one way, rated difficult, from the trailhead at the end of forest road 626, reached by driving 9.4 miles on Highway 75 from Stanley. No water on the trail. Watch the weather: the summit is dangerous in lightning storms.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Sawtooth National Recreation Area per NHLR)

events.note: The later restorer was a former lookout staff member in 1961 (NHLR); which lookout he staffed is not stated in the sources read.
Moved to emergency status in the 1970s; firelookout.com says used for emergencies into the 1970s.
Slated to be burned; a former 1961 lookout contacted the Forest Service and the cab was saved from demolition.
Restored by a former 1961 lookout staff member: repaired hardwood floors, door, two shutters, catwalk and steps, and painted.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on November 27, 2016; nominated by Luke Channer.

corrections.why: The record's 3024.5 m matches NHLR's 9,923 ft (3,025 m). Idaho Fire Lookouts, firelookout.com and Wikipedia all give 9,954 ft, which is 3,034 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 9,923 ft (3,025 m); Idaho Fire Lookouts, firelookout.com and Wikipedia give 9,954 ft (3,034 m). Three sources agree on the higher figure, so the proposed correction follows them.

NHLR places the lookout in the Sawtooth National Recreation Area and lists the U.S. Forest Service as administrator; Idaho Fire Lookouts names the Salmon-Challis National Forest. The story uses the Sawtooth NRA wording, which NHLR and Wikipedia both support.

Wikipedia says the lookout was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps and was recently refurbished. NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com do not say who built it, so the story leaves the CCC claim out.

notes_for_editor: The 1933 build year and the 1985-89 save-and-restore story agree across NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts. Elevation and forest name conflict across sources (see resolved_conflicts). Wikipedia's CCC claim is unconfirmed by the register or the other lists; check Wikipedia's refs before adding it. Do not confuse with other Lookout Mountain towers: Idaho Fire Lookouts' west-central 'Lookout Mountain Lookout' (1933 14x14 log cabin, moved 1975) and its northern-Idaho Lookout Mountain are different sites. The trail is a difficult hike and the summit is a lightning hazard; the cab itself is on emergency status. No notable fires were found in the sources read. NHLR photos (courtesy Luke Channer) have no licence shown, so none are listed. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1961 staffing event no longer implies this tower was staffed that year; the story no longer says the trail went 'up' the forest road.
